question: What is the main goal of debulking surgery for ovarian cancer?

options.A: To preserve the uterus and ovaries for future childbearing
options.B: To completely cure the patient without needing chemotherapy
options.C: To remove as much visible tumor mass from the abdomen as possible
options.D: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests

explanation: Spot on! Leaving behind as little tumor as possible makes the follow-up chemotherapy much more effective. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h7)

question: How do money worries directly affect a patient who has been given a referral?

options.A: Patients may refuse or delay going because they cannot afford hospital fees
options.B: Hospitals automatically waive all bills for referred community patients
options.C: The government refunds transport money upon arrival at the gate
options.D: Patients receive double the amount of free drugs to compensate

explanation: So true. Because many people pay out-of-pocket, financial hardship often forces vulnerable patients to stay home instead of getting the specialist care they need. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for processing fear and triggering our fight-or-flight alarm?

options.A: Medulla oblongata
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Amygdala
options.D: Pituitary gland

explanation: Think of the amygdala as your brain's emotional smoke detector. It spots danger and sounds the alarm right away! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks when assessing a patient's personal host status?

options.A: Screening for underlying chronic illnesses like diabetes
options.B: Inquiring about recent travel history to endemic regions
options.C: Reviewing the patient's personal immunization records
options.D: Analyzing the genetic makeup of the local water supply

explanation: Host assessment is all about the *person* sitting in front of you—their health, vaccines, and history. Water genetics belong to environmental health, not individual patient assessment! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h6)

question: What is the primary function of GABA in the central nervous system?

options.A: To trigger happy memories in the frontal lobe
options.B: To stimulate muscle movement in the arms and legs
options.C: To calm nervous system activity and reduce anxiety
options.D: To increase blood pressure during a physical threat

explanation: GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter, meaning it slows down brain activity to keep anxiety levels manageable. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why do nurses keep doing frequent neuro checks for unstable patients?

options.A: To catch early signs of rising intracranial pressure
options.B: To ensure the patient stays awake all night long
options.C: To keep the patient's family members from worrying
options.D: To prevent the patient from asking too many questions

explanation: Things can change fast in acute care. Frequent checks help you catch warning signs of pressure in the brain early, way before serious damage happens. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the difference between intragroup and intergroup conflict?

options.A: Intragroup involves money, while intergroup involves medical errors.
options.B: Intragroup happens within the same team, while intergroup happens between different teams.
options.C: Intragroup is internal, while intergroup is external.
options.D: Intragroup only occurs at night, while intergroup occurs during the day.

explanation: Think of 'intra-' as *within* one group, and 'inter-' as *between* separate groups. Easy trick to remember! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h4)

question: A nurse gets a positive rapid malaria test for a pregnant woman in a remote village. What should happen next?

options.A: Tell her to return home and wait for the fever to disappear on its own
options.B: Initiate the appropriate anti-malarial treatment protocol immediately
options.C: Ignore the result because rapid tests are never accurate
options.D: Send her patient file directly to the international health organization

explanation: Testing is only helpful if we act on the results! Once malaria is confirmed, starting treatment right away keeps both mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h5)

question: If clinic data shows a high rate of patients stopping their birth control, how can a nurse use this to help?

options.A: By ignoring the data since statistics do not affect daily bedside nursing
options.B: By stopping all contraceptive distribution until the government intervenes
options.C: By strengthening pre-conception counseling and managing side effects proactively
options.D: By discharging patients who request a change in their birth control method

explanation: People usually stop using birth control because of side effects. If we counsel them well beforehand and manage those side effects early, they are much more likely to stick with it! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T027#GNS226_U6_T027_h8)

question: Why do safety experts encourage a blame-free reporting culture in hospitals?

options.A: It encourages staff to report errors so systems can be fixed
options.B: It allows managers to punish careless workers more easily
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever making mistakes again
options.D: It stops patients from filing lawsuits against the hospital

explanation: Spot on! When nurses aren't afraid of being punished, they speak up about close calls. That honesty helps the whole team fix dangerous workflows. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why must a gravity drainage bag always be positioned below the level of the wound?

options.A: To use gravity to pull fluid out and prevent it from flowing back
options.B: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.C: To keep the collection bag hidden from the patient's direct view
options.D: To stop the tubing from becoming permanently kinked or twisted

explanation: If the collection container is higher than the wound, fluid inside the tubing can flow backward into the body cavity, introducing bacteria and causing infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h2)

question: Which of these best describes an operating system (OS)?

options.A: A physical input device used to scan patient identification bands
options.B: Physical memory chips that temporarily hold data while you type
options.C: Core software that manages computer hardware and provides a user interface
options.D: A specialized mobile app used exclusively for calculating medication dosages

explanation: The OS is the grand manager (like Windows or Android) that lets you talk to the computer hardware and run your favorite apps. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: When does a conflict of interest typically occur in a healthcare setting?

options.A: When an individual worker's goals clash directly with the demands of the health facility
options.B: When all nurses and doctors agree on the exact same shift roster
options.C: When the hospital has an excess of funds and medical supplies
options.D: When patient satisfaction scores reach one hundred percent

explanation: Conflict happens when what you want to do (like resting or traveling) clashes with what the hospital urgently needs you to do (like covering a busy shift). [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h6)

question: In research language, what is a 'sampling frame'?

options.A: A framework for writing up the final research report
options.B: The physical room where patient interviews take place
options.C: A complete list of everyone in the accessible population
options.D: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size

explanation: Think of a sampling frame as your phone book or registry list. It's the actual directory of names you draw your participants from! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h4)

question: A nurse researcher wants to check if there is a link between water source type and the prevalence of cholera in a community. Which study type is best?

options.A: Qualitative interview study
options.B: Analytical cross-sectional study
options.C: Purely descriptive case report
options.D: Longitudinal clinical trial

explanation: When you are looking for a connection between two things at one specific time, an analytical cross-sectional study is your best friend. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h3)

question: A chronic disease has very few new cases each year, yet a high number of people live with it for decades. What will the statistics show?

options.A: Low incidence and high prevalence
options.B: Both incidence and prevalence will be equal
options.C: Both incidence and prevalence will be zero
options.D: High incidence and low prevalence

explanation: Few new cases mean low incidence, but long-term survival accumulates existing cases, resulting in high prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: An outsourced cleaning company constantly fails to clean the wards on time. What should hospital management do?

options.A: Ignore the issue to maintain a peaceful relationship with the private company
options.B: Review the service-level agreement and hold the vendor accountable for breaches
options.C: Ask nursing staff to take over all cleaning duties permanently without extra support
options.D: Immediately terminate all public-private partnerships across the entire country

explanation: When vendors slack off, management must check the agreed contract terms and hold them accountable—just like in any business relationship! [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h7)

question: How does a 'just culture' help a hospital reduce unwanted variation in care?

options.A: By punishing anyone who deviates from standard hospital routine
options.B: By ensuring every nurse receives the exact same annual salary bonus
options.C: By removing all nursing supervisors from clinical hospital wards
options.D: By encouraging staff to report workflow issues and near-misses safely

explanation: You're a star! A just culture builds trust so nurses feel safe speaking up about problems before anyone gets hurt. Keep up the awesome work! [learn more](GST319_U2_T4#GST319_U2_T4_h6)

question: What do we call the situation where cities have plenty of health workers while rural villages have very few?

options.A: Comprehensive deployment
options.B: Epidemiological transition
options.C: Geographic maldistribution
options.D: Horizontal integration

explanation: Maldistribution simply means healthcare workers are unevenly spread out across the map, usually clustering in comfortable urban centers. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main job of a healthy fallopian tube?

options.A: To filter waste products from the pelvic cavity
options.B: To provide a pathway for the egg and the site for fertilization
options.C: To produce female hormones like estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To nourish the developing embryo throughout the entire pregnancy

explanation: Think of the fallopian tube as the highway where the egg travels and meets sperm for fertilization. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of agricultural subsidies provided by the government?

options.A: To lower production risks and support farmers
options.B: To replace natural rainfall with artificial irrigation everywhere
options.C: To increase the retail price of basic food items
options.D: To punish farmers who grow traditional local crops

explanation: Subsidies help farmers manage financial and environmental risks so they can keep producing food reliably. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: Which Nigerian body is in charge of registering nurses and looking after our professional discipline?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is our very own guardian angel body set up by law to guide nursing training and practice right here in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h2)

question: A newborn is born limp, pale, and not breathing. What should be your very first immediate action in resuscitation?

options.A: Clear the airway and position the head correctly
options.B: Clamp and cut the cord immediately
options.C: Administer intravenous antibiotics right away
options.D: Weigh the baby on the delivery scale

explanation: Effective resuscitation begins with proper head positioning and clearing the airway to ensure air can enter the lungs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h7)

question: A patient comes in with sudden fever and body pains. Why does a nurse care about the incubation period?

options.A: To count backward and figure out when they likely got infected
options.B: To guess how much water the patient lost from sweating
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To know the exact brand of drugs to prescribe

explanation: Knowing a disease's timeline helps nurses play detective to pinpoint when and where the patient caught the bug. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h4)

question: How deep should your chest compressions be when doing high-quality CPR on an adult?

options.A: Five centimeters minimum
options.B: One-half inch maximum
options.C: At least two inches
options.D: Exactly four inches

explanation: You're doing great. To squeeze that heart enough to push blood out, you need to press down at least two inches deep! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h4)

question: Who serves as the vital link between frontline nursing care and software developers?

options.A: Pharmacy technicians
options.B: Hospital billing clerks
options.C: Nurse informaticians
options.D: Biomedical electricians

explanation: Exactly right! Nurse informaticians combine real bedside nursing experience with computer science to help design better healthcare tech. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is it important to teach patients to finish all prescribed drops even if they feel better?

options.A: Stopping early can allow the infection to return stronger
options.B: Unused drops will expire quickly on the bathroom shelf
options.C: Leftover drops can cause severe poisoning if saved
options.D: Doctors require empty bottles brought back to the clinic

explanation: Stopping medication early before all bacteria or inflammation is cleared often causes the condition to flare up again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h9)

question: A stroke patient has weak arms on one side, but she can still wash her face if her wash basin is placed close by. What should you do?

options.A: Tell her family to do all her bathing when they visit
options.B: Wait until her full strength returns before she bathes
options.C: Encourage her to wash her upper body while you assist with the rest
options.D: Do everything for her to save her energy

explanation: Wonderful choice! Encouraging whatever independence a patient has left boosts their mood and helps them recover faster. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the best immediate nursing action for an unconscious patient who is breathing on their own?

options.A: Force fluids by mouth to prevent dehydration during sleep
options.B: Place them in the recovery position to keep the airway clear
options.C: Prop them upright in bed to encourage deep lung breathing
options.D: Tie their arms to the bed rails to prevent sudden movement

explanation: The recovery position keeps the tongue from blocking the airway and lets saliva drain out safely. A classic life-saving nursing skill! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is a major systemic challenge facing health promotion programs in Nigeria?

options.A: An extreme surplus of modern medical equipment in rural areas
options.B: Too many well-funded hospitals with no patients to treat
options.C: Brain drain of skilled healthcare professionals leaving the country
options.D: Zero interest from local communities in improving their health

explanation: The migration of experienced doctors and nurses abroad significantly weakens local healthcare delivery systems and health promotion efforts. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: As a psychiatric nurse, why is it so helpful to look beyond a patient's immediate symptoms?

options.A: Because medication orders are written by the hospital pharmacist
options.B: So the patient can be discharged within twenty-four hours
options.C: To diagnose physical infections causing a fever
options.D: To understand the broader ecosystem and life background

explanation: People don't live in a vacuum! Understanding their family, home life, and background helps you see the real root causes of their struggles. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of these actions directly targets the environmental cause of a waterborne disease?

options.A: Conducting door-to-door census surveys
options.B: Administering therapeutic vitamins
options.C: Chlorinating public water supplies
options.D: Isolating patients in hospital wards

explanation: Chlorine cleans the water supply, stopping harmful germs right at the source before they reach anyone's cup. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h5)

question: What is the ultimate goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC)?

options.A: Ensuring everyone gets needed health services without financial hardship
options.B: Making all hospitals in the country completely free and private
options.C: Eliminating the need for nurses and doctors in rural areas
options.D: Requiring every citizen to travel abroad for complex surgeries

explanation: UHC simply means everyone can walk into a hospital, get quality treatment, and not go broke doing it. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which type of measure checks if the specific steps of a new plan are actually being carried out on the ward?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Financial measure
options.D: Balancing measure

explanation: You're doing great! Process measures help us check whether we are consistently doing the actual tasks we planned to do. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient experiences severe dehydration. What immediate effect does this have on body function?

options.A: Sudden increase in muscle mass and bone density
options.B: Immediate conversion of fats into stored carbohydrates
options.C: Disruption of metabolic processes and electrolyte balance
options.D: Rapid overproduction of digestive enzymes in the gut

explanation: Without enough water, blood volume drops, electrolytes concentrate abnormally, and cellular chemical reactions slow down or fail. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h4)

question: Where does developing true cultural competence in nursing actually begin?

options.A: Reading advanced textbooks on international medical laws
options.B: Memorizing every religious holiday observed in the country
options.C: Traveling to foreign countries to study local hospital systems
options.D: Recognizing one's own personal biases and cultural assumptions

explanation: Spot on! Self-awareness is key. You first have to understand your own background and biases so they don't mess with the care you give others. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h7)

question: What makes ethical choices so emotionally heavy for nurses during a major disaster?

options.A: Having to ration scarce life-saving resources among many needy patients
options.B: Having too many modern medical machines to choose from
options.C: Working in fully air-conditioned and quiet field offices
options.D: Patients having unlimited time to discuss treatment options

explanation: So true. Deciding who gets scarce life-saving care when there isn't enough to go around is one of the hardest emotional burdens a nurse can carry. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h10)

question: What was the main purpose of early almshouses and poorhouses?

options.A: To provide advanced surgical and medical treatments
options.B: To train the first generation of registered nurses
options.C: To serve as specialized retirement homes for the wealthy
options.D: To shelter the destitute, elderly, and chronically ill

explanation: Think of early almshouses as general community shelters. They were set up to care for people who had no one else, like the poor and frail elderly, long before modern hospitals and nursing homes existed! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of quantitative clinical data?

options.A: Monthly count of medication administration errors
options.B: Handwritten notes from a shift handover meeting
options.C: Subjective feedback about hospital meal quality
options.D: Patient narrative descriptions of their pain experience

explanation: Remember, quantitative data has to do with quantities and numbers! Counting how many medication errors happened in a month gives you hard numbers. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h2)

question: How does regular physical exercise help lower a person's blood sugar?

options.A: By permanently curing pancreatic beta cell damage
options.B: By destroying excess sugar in the bloodstream
options.C: By increasing insulin sensitivity in muscle cells
options.D: By slowing down overall body metabolism

explanation: Exercise tunes up your muscle cells so they respond better to insulin, helping them pull glucose out of the blood much easier. Keep up the momentum! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h6)

question: Why are patients with surgical wounds or catheters at higher risk if equipment is poorly decontaminated?

options.A: They usually stay in the hospital longer than other patients do
options.B: They produce more body heat which helps bacteria multiply faster
options.C: Their immune systems completely stop working during recovery
options.D: Their natural body barriers are breached, allowing germs to enter easily

explanation: Surgical wounds and catheters bypass the body's normal physical defenses, providing a direct entry point for pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: When would a clinician choose indirect ophthalmoscopy over direct ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: When performing a quick bedside neurological check on a ward
options.B: When examining the far periphery of the entire retina
options.C: When only a small portion of the central optic disc needs viewing
options.D: When the patient cannot tolerate any bright light shining near them

explanation: Indirect ophthalmoscopy provides a much wider, stereoscopic view that allows the examiner to see the far edges of the retina. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h3)

question: What key role do community health nurses play when working with incoming NGO teams?

options.A: Managing financial audits for donor agencies
options.B: Funding the operational budgets of international organizations
options.C: Acting as a liaison to coordinate outreach schedules with local clinics
options.D: Drafting national health legislation in the federal assembly

explanation: Nurses are the vital bridge between visiting NGOs and local primary health centers, keeping patient care organized and steady. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h5)

question: What is the main goal of setting up a national health insurance program?

options.A: To replace all doctors with automated medical software
options.B: To achieve nationwide access to healthcare for all citizens
options.C: To restrict healthcare services to high-income earners
options.D: To make public hospitals entirely self-funding

explanation: Well done! National schemes are designed to give every citizen, especially vulnerable groups, fair and easy access to essential medical services. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is a common myth about medication administration errors?

options.A: They only occur in busy surgical operating rooms
options.B: They are always the sole fault of the nurse at the bedside
options.C: They never result in any negative physical outcomes
options.D: They are completely eliminated by electronic health records

explanation: Even though the nurse gives the drug, the root cause might actually go back to prescribing, pharmacy dispensing, or unclear packaging! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h5)

question: A patient eats a snack with 10g of carbs, 5g of protein, and 4g of fat. What is their total calorie intake?

options.A: 60 kcal
options.B: 96 kcal
options.C: 76 kcal
options.D: 19 kcal

explanation: Let's break it down: Carbs (10 x 4 = 40), Protein (5 x 4 = 20), Fat (4 x 9 = 36). Add them up (40 + 20 + 36) to get 96 total calories. You're doing great with math! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h3)

question: Why is a single initial assessment insufficient for palliative care patients?

options.A: Palliative conditions and symptoms change rapidly over time
options.B: Patients usually forget their medical history on day one
options.C: Doctors prefer to change diagnoses daily without reason
options.D: Hospitals require a new paperwork form every single hour

explanation: Because disease trajectories fluctuate, ongoing re-assessment is necessary to catch new or worsening symptoms. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h2)

question: What happens to vital body proteins if the blood pH moves way outside the normal range?

options.A: They multiply rapidly to restore chemical balance
options.B: They convert directly into usable cellular energy
options.C: They bind permanently to excess sodium molecules
options.D: They denature and lose their functional shape

explanation: Proteins are picky! When blood gets too acidic or too basic, proteins change shape (denature) and stop working properly, which halts important body processes. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h2)

question: On a standard nursing line graph, what does the horizontal line (X-axis) usually show?

options.A: The name of the attending nurse
options.B: Time, such as days or months
options.C: The total cost of patient care
options.D: The exact blood pressure reading

explanation: You got it! The X-axis runs flat across the bottom and is almost always used to map out the passage of time. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T10#GNS217_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the main idea behind a Public-Private Partnership (PPP)?

options.A: Military defense tactics and nursing education
options.B: Traditional herbal medicine and spiritual healing
options.C: Foreign travel agencies and local pharmacies
options.D: Government authority and private sector efficiency

explanation: A PPP combines the rules and backing of the government with the speed and business skills of the private sector to get things done. [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h5)

question: How do public health nurses figure out how long a quarantine period should last for people exposed to a disease?

options.A: By waiting until laboratory cultures turn completely negative
options.B: By keeping contacts isolated for a standard seven days
options.C: By looking at the maximum incubation period of the disease
options.D: By measuring the patient's exact body temperature daily

explanation: Spot on! Quarantine matches the longest known incubation time so we can catch any potential new cases before people mingle. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why are standard gravity IV drips unreliable in a moving ambulance?

options.A: Changing road angles and vehicle motion alter the fluid flow rate
options.B: Plastic IV bags automatically dissolve when exposed to engine exhaust
options.C: The vibration makes the fluid change its chemical composition
options.D: Nurses are legally forbidden from using bags inside vehicles

explanation: As the ambulance accelerates, brakes, and turns corners, the angle of the fluid relative to the patient shifts, making infusion pumps much safer. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h5)

question: When introducing a new practice to a unit, why is it so helpful to involve local peer champions?

options.A: Peer champions are the only staff members legally allowed to train others
options.B: Local champions work longer hours without extra pay than regular nurses
options.C: Staff trust and follow respected colleagues more readily than distant managers
options.D: Hospital policy requires a peer champion to sign off on every patient chart

explanation: As student nurses, we know we look up to our senior colleagues and trusted peers for guidance. Peer influence is a powerful tool for positive change! [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h4)

question: What do we call skin changes that show up directly as the very first sign of a disease process?

options.A: Vascular lesions
options.B: Primary lesions
options.C: Purpuric lesions
options.D: Secondary lesions

explanation: Spotting primary lesions helps you catch skin conditions right at the beginning before they change. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h1)

question: When is a public health nurse legally and ethically permitted to breach patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the local newspaper offers financial payment for health records
options.B: When the patient's condition poses an immediate and severe threat to public safety
options.C: Whenever a curious neighbor asks about someone's medical diagnosis
options.D: Whenever the nurse feels like gossiping during lunch break

explanation: Confidentiality is a sacred duty, but protecting the public from severe, imminent harm overrides individual privacy rights under specific legal guidelines. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is the main way Metformin helps lower blood sugar in the body?

options.A: Stimulating the beta cells of the pancreas to release stored insulin
options.B: Slowing down the digestion of carbohydrates in the small intestine
options.C: Decreasing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity
options.D: Blocking the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules

explanation: Exactly right! Metformin tells the liver to ease up on making extra sugar and helps your body's cells respond better to your natural insulin. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h4)

question: Why is the recovery phase just as important as the active response phase?

options.A: It is the only time nurses are legally allowed to administer medications.
options.B: It helps the community rebuild infrastructure and restore long-term health.
options.C: It prevents disasters from ever happening again in the future.
options.D: It replaces the need for any pre-disaster planning or drills.

explanation: Exactly! Recovery is all about long-term healing, fixing damaged buildings, and supporting the mental health of survivors over months or years. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h3)

question: When is empiric antibiotic therapy usually started for a sick patient?

options.A: Only when the exact microscopic species is confirmed
options.B: After the patient is fully discharged from the hospital
options.C: When the patient shows an allergic reaction to skin tests
options.D: Before laboratory culture results return from the lab

explanation: Empiric treatment gives a patient immediate help based on clinical signs while we wait for the lab results to come back. Great to know for ward practice! [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is an elevated pulse often considered an early warning sign of patient distress?

options.A: The heart speeds up to compensate before blood pressure drops
options.B: Fever always causes immediate kidney failure if left untreated
options.C: It proves the patient is simply feeling nervous about hospital food
options.D: A fast pulse means the lungs have stopped absorbing oxygen entirely

explanation: The body increases the heart rate to maintain adequate blood flow and pressure when stress, blood loss, or illness occurs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: A patient with a complex heart condition that a local general hospital cannot manage is most likely sent to which level?

question: What is a major reason why mothers in rural areas struggle to attend infant welfare clinics?

options.A: Mandatory fees that exceed hospital costs
options.B: Long distance and lack of transport
options.C: Excessive availability of private doctors
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting clinic visits

explanation: You got it! Living far away with bad transport options makes it really tough for rural mums to travel to a clinic regularly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h7)

question: Why do babies with sickle cell anaemia usually look completely healthy at birth?

options.A: The bone marrow does not produce red blood cells until the age of one
options.B: Infant blood vessels are too wide for blockages to possibly form
options.C: The mother's immune system filters out all the abnormal blood cells
options.D: High levels of fetal haemoglobin protect the red blood cells temporarily

explanation: Fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is tough and resists sickling. It's only when HbF starts dropping after birth that symptoms begin to show up. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is the nurse's role so crucial for making a National Drug Policy work in real life?

options.A: Nurses are solely responsible for importing essential medicines from international manufacturers.
options.B: Nurses are the frontline professionals who handle, administer, and educate patients about medications daily.
options.C: Nurses hold the legal authority to shut down illegal open-air drug markets across the country.
options.D: Nurses write the legal statutes that govern pharmaceutical practice in government courts.

explanation: Policies are just paper until we put them into practice! Because nurses handle, give, and teach about drugs every day, our actions make the policy a success. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why must a nurse pull back the clothes and actually look at the patient's bare chest during a breathing assessment?

options.A: To listen for tummy sounds in the chest
options.B: To check the exact skin temperature
options.C: To check for chest symmetry, injuries, and odd movements
options.D: To get the skin ready for ECG stickers

explanation: Exactly! Looking closely helps you spot uneven chest rise, hidden wounds, or flail segments that make breathing difficult. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is an UNSAFE way to thaw frozen meat?

options.A: Using the defrost setting on a microwave oven
options.B: Submerging it securely in cold running tap water
options.C: Leaving it on the kitchen counter at room temperature
options.D: Thawing it slowly inside the refrigerator compartment

explanation: You nailed it! Leaving meat on the counter lets the outside warm up into the danger zone where bacteria love to multiply. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h5)

question: What is the main difference between the scope of practice of an LPN and a home health aide?

options.A: LPNs only handle housekeeping duties while aides manage complex wounds
options.B: Aides are licensed to supervise registered nurses in the home setting
options.C: LPNs can perform routine clinical tasks like giving medications, while aides focus on personal care
options.D: There is no difference in training or clinical responsibilities

explanation: LPNs have nursing training that allows them to handle basic clinical interventions, whereas home health aides are restricted to personal support tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: How can an unsterile instrument used during an abortion lead to septic shock?

options.A: By introducing bacteria that multiply and spread into the bloodstream
options.B: By causing an immediate allergic reaction inside the womb
options.C: By cutting off oxygen to the major abdominal organs
options.D: By causing a sudden drop in blood pressure purely from pain

explanation: Unclean tools carry germs straight into the womb, causing a severe infection that can enter the bloodstream and trigger shock. You're mastering the basics of sepsis! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to treat drinking water?

options.A: Adding appropriate chlorine treatment
options.B: Boiling it thoroughly
options.C: Storing it uncovered in a warm, dusty corner
options.D: Using a certified water filtration system

explanation: Exactly! Leaving clean water uncovered is an open invitation for dust, flies, and germs to sneak right back in and contaminate it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h5)

question: Which type of quality measure looks directly at the final clinical result or health status of a patient?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Financial measure

explanation: Spot on! Outcome measures check the final destination—like whether the patient's infection cleared up or how well they are recovering. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing a hysterosalpingography test during an infertility workup?

options.A: To count the total number of immature eggs remaining in the ovaries
options.B: To check the thyroid gland for signs of overactivity
options.C: To visualize the uterine cavity and check if fallopian tubes are open
options.D: To measure the exact daily progesterone levels in the blood

explanation: Awesome job! During this test, dye is put through the cervix so x-rays can show if the fluid flows nicely through the tubes. You're building solid practical knowledge! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h6)

question: Why should a nurse researcher investigate an outlier rather than deleting it immediately?

options.A: Outliers always improve the accuracy of statistical tests
options.B: It proves that the measurement scale was ordinal
options.C: Deleting data is illegal in all health research
options.D: It might represent a genuine, important clinical finding

explanation: An extreme value might look like an error at first glance, but it could actually reflect a real, critical clinical event that deserves attention. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of triage when a mass casualty happens?

options.A: Sending all injured persons immediately to the operating theatre
options.B: Ensuring every single patient receives equal amounts of time
options.C: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people
options.D: Treating the most critically ill patient before anyone else

explanation: Great thinking! When supplies and staff are limited, triage helps us save as many lives as possible by prioritizing resources wisely. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h2)

question: When dealing with adolescent confidentiality dilemmas, what is the nurse's main responsibility?

options.A: Instantly reporting every minor to local law enforcement authorities
options.B: Refusing to treat any patient under the age of eighteen years
options.C: Breaching privacy whenever a family member asks for details
options.D: Balancing client safety and health rights with ethical and legal realities

explanation: Nurses must carefully weigh a minor's right to privacy against legal duties and immediate safety concerns. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h8)

question: Why is it extra important to secure an endotracheal tube firmly during a medical evacuation?

options.A: Air pressure changes automatically deflate the tube cuff
options.B: Vehicle jolts and movement can easily dislodge the airway
options.C: Ambient engine noise prevents nurses from hearing breath sounds
options.D: High altitudes cause the plastic tubing to melt quickly

explanation: Bumpy roads and turbulence can easily bump a tube out of place. Securing it tightly prevents accidental removal when you're far from a hospital. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h6)

question: How do routine clinic records generated from standing orders benefit the wider public health system?

options.A: They replace the need for community health educational campaigns
options.B: They guarantee that hospitals never run out of surgical equipment
options.C: They allow the federal government to tax private patent medicine vendors
options.D: They provide data that helps health authorities track disease trends and manage drug stocks

explanation: Aggregated clinic records show disease patterns, helping authorities monitor outbreaks and plan medical supply chains effectively. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h7)

question: What do we call the basic grid system of rows and columns in Excel?

options.A: A word processor
options.B: A database table
options.C: A presentation slide
options.D: A spreadsheet

explanation: Excel is all about spreadsheets! The rows and columns give you a neat grid to organize and crunch numbers easily. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: A nurse manager tries out a new handoff checklist with one shift, collects feedback, and compares results to what she predicted. Which PDSA phase is she in?

options.A: Plan
options.B: Study
options.C: Do
options.D: Act

explanation: She is in the 'Study' phase! This is where you look at the data you collected and check how closely it matches your original predictions. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h2)

question: An infant is brought to the clinic for routine immunization at 9 months old. Which key vaccine is due at this visit?

options.A: Measles vaccine
options.B: Pentavalent booster dose four
options.C: First dose of BCG
options.D: Oral polio vaccine dose zero

explanation: Spot on! The first dose of the measles vaccine is scheduled right at 9 months to keep growing babies safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why should a nurse designer limit a health poster to just one or two main actions?

options.A: Health workers do not have time to memorize long lists of instructions.
options.B: Paper becomes too heavy and expensive to distribute easily.
options.C: Government printing presses refuse to print more than two sentences.
options.D: Too many competing messages confuse the audience and dilute the impact.

explanation: Keep it simple! If you put too many instructions on one poster, people get overwhelmed and walk away remembering nothing. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: How does handwashing help stop the spread of infection?

options.A: By interrupting how germs travel from place to place
options.B: By sealing up the tiny pores on the outer skin
options.C: By making the patient completely immune to diseases
options.D: By clearing germs from inside the body's main organs

explanation: Exactly! Washing your hands washes away germs so they can't hitch a ride to your next patient. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why do we need a team of different healthcare workers at the primary health care level?

options.A: Community members prefer being treated by multiple practitioners at once
options.B: Different health professionals are needed to cover diverse community needs
options.C: Hospital doctors refuse to travel outside urban administrative centers
options.D: Government policies require high staff counts to justify operational budgets

explanation: A community has all sorts of needs—from immunizations to health talks and treating minor illnesses. No single profession can do it all alone! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h1)

question: When dressing a stroke patient with weakness on one side, where should you put the clothes first?

options.A: Whichever side they prefer
options.B: The strong or unaffected side
options.C: Both sides at the exact same time
options.D: The weak or affected side

explanation: Brilliant! Dressing the weak side first saves the patient from painful, awkward twisting of a limb that lacks strength. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h5)

question: After gathering your data and setting priorities, what is the most important final output to create?

options.A: A practical action plan with goals, responsibilities, and timelines
options.B: An indefinite suspension of all community health outreaches
options.C: A private financial statement kept hidden from community leaders
options.D: A complex textbook filled with heavy medical Latin terms

explanation: Data is only helpful if we use it! Turning your findings into a clear, organized action plan guides your next steps as a nurse. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a review of systems during an interview?

options.A: To perform a complete hands-on physical examination
options.B: To diagnose every chronic disease the patient has
options.C: To test the patient's knowledge of anatomy and physiology
options.D: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or omitted

explanation: You got it! The review of systems acts as a helpful safety net to catch any symptoms the patient forgot to mention. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h7)

question: How many months of cycle tracking are generally recommended before relying on the calendar method?

options.A: Only one single month
options.B: Six to twelve months
options.C: Five whole years
options.D: Exactly two weeks

explanation: Tracking past cycles for several months helps you find a reliable pattern of your shortest and longest cycles, which is needed for the math to work out! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h2)

question: A mother calls because her 2-day-old baby is super sleepy and won't feed at all. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.A: A mild milk allergy needing a brand change
options.B: Normal newborn behavior that will fix itself
options.C: A serious hidden problem needing urgent medical review
options.D: Just normal tiredness from growing

explanation: Lethargy and refusing to feed are major warning signs in babies. It could point to infection, low blood sugar, or dehydration—always treat it as urgent! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h9)

question: Why should the nurse advise a patient to bring sunglasses to their ophthalmoscopy appointment?

options.A: Bright sunlight blocks the dilating drops from working properly
options.B: Dilated pupils let in excess light, causing glare and discomfort outdoors
options.C: Sunglasses protect the delicate contact lenses from blowing dust outside
options.D: The bright examination room light permanently damages unshielded eyes

explanation: Because dilating drops keep the pupil wide open, natural sunlight becomes overwhelmingly bright and uncomfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: A patient with a tummy bug is passing watery stool. Which body system is acting as the portal of exit?

options.A: Cardiovascular system
options.B: Gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Integumentary system
options.D: Respiratory tract

explanation: Spot on! Stool and digestive issues come from the GI tract, making it the exit route for tummy bugs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which clinical finding shows up early in a measles infection?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Painful spasms of the jaw muscles
options.C: Koplik spots inside the oral cavity
options.D: A thick grey membrane in the throat

explanation: Spot on! Koplik spots look like tiny grains of salt on a red background inside the cheeks, and they are a dead giveaway for early measles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h5)

question: What is the largest and longest nerve in the human body?

options.A: Median nerve
options.B: Femoral nerve
options.C: Sciatic nerve
options.D: Phrenic nerve

explanation: The sciatic nerve is the largest single nerve in the body, arising from the sacral plexus and supplying the lower limbs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h7)

question: What fluid should you use to flush the IV tubing after a blood transfusion is complete?

options.D: Sterile Water for Injection

question: Which item belongs inside the yellow infectious waste bin during an immunization session?

options.A: Food wrappers left over from the outreach lunch break
options.B: Cardboard packaging boxes that held the vaccine vials
options.C: Cotton swabs stained with blood or vaccine fluid
options.D: Empty plastic water bottles brought by clinic staff

explanation: Items contaminated with body fluids or biological residues must go into biohazard infectious bins to prevent contamination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: A hospital needs a powerful system to manage records for thousands of patients at the same time. Which type of computer is best suited for this?

options.A: A single pocket calculator
options.B: A simple analog wave measuring tool
options.C: A large central system like a mainframe
options.D: A basic desktop microcomputer with no network

explanation: You got it! Mainframes are the heavy lifters of the hospital world, built to handle massive networks and data for entire institutions all at once. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the top nursing priority right after major cancer surgery?

options.A: Withdrawing all intravenous fluids immediately
options.B: Preventing complications and managing acute surgical pain
options.C: Discharging the patient within twenty-four hours
options.D: Starting intensive physical exercise right away

explanation: Right after surgery, keeping your patient comfortable and watching out for issues like infection or blood clots are your most important duties. You are well on your way to becoming an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical workplace stressor that puts nurses at risk?

options.A: Fatigue from rotating shift work disrupting normal sleep patterns
options.B: Chronic understaffing and heavy patient dependency loads
options.C: Exposure to traumatic patient deaths and emergency situations
options.D: Guaranteed 40-hour work weeks with zero night shifts

explanation: Predictable shifts with regular hours wouldn't cause the extreme burnout and exhaustion linked to nurse fatigue. If only every ward schedule was this nice! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h2)

question: A patient living near a fast-flowing river presents with severe skin itching and early vision changes. Which insect is most likely the culprit?

options.A: Sandfly
options.B: Housefly
options.C: Blackfly
options.D: Louse

explanation: Blackflies love fast-flowing rivers and are notorious for spreading the worms that cause river blindness (onchocerciasis). Good clinical deduction! [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do hospitals look at medication errors as system problems rather than just blaming the individual nurse?

options.A: Because doctors are legally responsible for every single pill a nurse hands out
options.B: Because regulatory agencies do not hold individual nurses accountable for errors
options.C: Because modern hospital computers prevent human nurses from making any wrong choices
options.D: Because poor workflows, fatigue, and confusing labels often set workers up for mistakes

explanation: Mistakes often happen because of tired shifts, busy wards, or confusing drug packaging. Fixing the workplace system keeps everyone safer, rather than just pointing fingers! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a major source of information when conducting a retrospective nursing study?

options.A: New clinical trials
options.B: Electronic health records
options.C: Live patient interviews
options.D: Real-time vital sign tracking

explanation: Correct! Since retrospective research relies on things that already happened, electronic health records (EHRs) are a goldmine for this kind of data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T14#GNS224_U1_T14_h3)

question: What makes a management audit unique compared to a financial audit?

options.A: Restricted to checking mathematical errors in ledgers
options.B: Forward-looking and focused on operational efficiency
options.C: Performed exclusively by external bank examiners
options.D: Conducts only legal trials for corrupt employees

explanation: You can think of financial audits as looking in the rearview mirror at past money, while management audits look forward to make daily hospital operations run better! [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h3)

question: A patient with a low CD4 count has creamy white patches in their mouth that bleed easily when scraped. What is this likely to be?

options.A: Cytomegalovirus ulcers
options.B: Oral hairy leukoplakia
options.C: Oral candidiasis
options.D: Herpes simplex stomatitis

explanation: Also known as oral thrush, these removable white plaques are very common when the immune system is deeply weakened. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h2)

question: Why is an individual patient's infection report important to the bigger picture of surveillance?

options.A: It proves the hospital has poor cleaning standards
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory testing
options.C: It guarantees that funding will increase for the ward
options.D: It helps public health teams spot community outbreaks early

explanation: Every single case serves as a vital data point that can signal the start of a wider spread of disease. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h1)

question: How do telehealth and home monitoring devices truly help patients living with chronic illnesses?

options.A: By lowering the financial cost of purchasing digital home appliances
options.B: By removing the need for patients to ever speak with a doctor again
options.C: By curing chronic diseases without the need for any prescription medications
options.D: By catching early warning signs before they turn into major emergencies

explanation: Spot on! Keeping a close eye on daily trends helps the care team step in before a small issue becomes a full-blown crisis. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which behavior is very common for a patient dealing with illness anxiety?

options.A: Consistently ignoring all physical pain without worry
options.B: Repeatedly checking the body for lumps or abnormalities
options.C: Voluntarily stopping all interactions with healthcare workers
options.D: Seeking immediate surgery for nonexistent conditions

explanation: You will often see patients engage in compulsive checking—like constantly scanning their skin, checking their pulse, or probing for swollen lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four parts of Deming's System of Profound Knowledge?

options.A: Knowledge of variation
options.B: Psychology
options.C: Financial accounting
options.D: Theory of knowledge

explanation: The four pillars are: system appreciation, variation, theory of knowledge, and psychology. Financial accounting is important business stuff, but not part of this specific framework! [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does strong teamwork help protect nurses from burnout?

options.A: Nurses are excused from direct bedside patient care duties
options.B: Hospital administrations eliminate all night shifts and weekend work
options.C: The heavy mental load of complex patient management is shared
options.D: Doctors take over all charting and documentation responsibilities

explanation: You got it! When the team shares responsibilities and talks things through, the heavy stress of patient care feels much lighter. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h4)

question: Which of these problems most commonly triggers an occlusion alarm on a syringe driver?

options.A: The correct programmed infusion rate
options.B: A normal room temperature reading
options.C: A fully charged battery in the pump
options.D: A kinked or blocked infusion tube

question: After losing their job, a person faces eviction, can no longer afford good food, and falls into deep depression. Which health areas are affected here?

options.A: Only the role performance dimension
options.B: Environmental, economic, emotional, and physical
options.C: Only the physical and intellectual dimensions
options.D: Strictly the spiritual and clinical dimensions

explanation: Fantastic! Life events don't happen in a vacuum. Losing a job touches housing (environmental), food (physical), money (economic), and mood (emotional) all at once. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why might a nurse or doctor collect a vulval tissue biopsy during an investigation?

options.A: To flush out trapped bacteria from the urinary bladder

options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels in the bloodstream
options.D: To check for chronic skin conditions or rule out abnormal cell changes

explanation: A biopsy sounds scary, but it's just a way for the lab to take a closer look at skin cells under a microscope when standard treatments aren't working. You're mastering diagnostic steps! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the cardiovascular system?

options.A: Moving nutrients throughout the body
options.B: Transporting oxygen to tissues
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes
options.D: Carrying carbon dioxide away from cells

explanation: Digestive enzymes are made by organs in your digestive system, like the pancreas and stomach, not your heart and blood vessels! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which common practice puts people at high risk for Lassa fever by letting rodents touch food?

options.A: Keeping domestic cats inside the main living areas at night
options.B: Drying food crops out in the open on mats or bare ground
options.C: Storing clean drinking water inside tightly sealed plastic containers
options.D: Washing cooking utensils immediately after every family meal

explanation: Spot on! Leaving grains exposed outside invites infected rats to contaminate them with their urine and droppings. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which hormone is secreted by the early trophoblast cells to signal pregnancy?

options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

question: A client tells you she always forgets to take daily medications. What should your counseling approach be?

options.A: Insist that she must take combined oral pills exactly at dawn every day
options.B: Recommend a method that does not require daily action, like injectables
options.C: Suggest she set an alarm and force herself to use oral pills
options.D: Tell her that family planning is not suitable for her lifestyle

explanation: Good nursing meets the client where she is! Matching her actual lifestyle to a method she can easily manage prevents frustration. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which medication is most commonly used as a local anesthetic for closing minor wounds?

options.A: Lignocaine
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Diazepam

explanation: Lignocaine numbs the local area quickly and safely when administered correctly before suturing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: What type of question should you ask if you want a patient to open up and share their feelings?

options.A: Rhetorical question
options.B: Closed-ended question
options.C: Open-ended question
options.D: Leading question

explanation: Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to talk in their own words, rather than just answering a quick 'yes' or 'no'. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the legal implication if you forget to chart a nursing care entry?

options.A: The hospital automatically wins any civil lawsuit
options.B: The doctor takes full responsibility for the missing note
options.C: The care is legally presumed not to have been performed
options.D: The nurse receives a bonus for saving paper

question: Why do resistant infections usually lead to much higher healthcare costs?

options.C: Laboratories must invent completely new testing equipment daily
options.D: Standard hospital disinfectants stop working on hospital floors

explanation: Think about it from a hospital perspective: when first-line drugs fail, patients need specialized care, extra days in bed, and much pricier backup medications. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h5)

question: What is a community diagnosis?

options.A: A laboratory test used to confirm typhoid fever
options.B: A prescription written for a patient with severe malaria
options.C: An official report written by the Minister of Health
options.D: An assessment of the overall health status of a population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at the health, living conditions, and resources of an entire group of people. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why do displaced persons living in crowded temporary camps often face sudden disease outbreaks?

options.A: A genetic predisposition unique to populations forced from their homes
options.B: Complete lack of exposure to any natural pathogens prior to displacement
options.C: The intentional release of biological agents within temporary settlement zones
options.D: Overcrowding combined with compromised sanitation and clean water shortages

explanation: Spot on! Tight spaces, lack of clean water, and poor waste disposal create the perfect storm for infections to spread quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which organ does the heavy lifting when it comes to adjusting and managing your daily fluid loss?

options.A: Lungs
options.B: Skin
options.C: Liver
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: Spot on! The kidneys are the ultimate fluid supervisors, tweaking how much water leaves your body every single day through urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h5)

question: How does knowing the difference between public and private providers help a nurse?

explanation: Brilliant! Going step-by-step from the head down ensures you never accidentally leave out an important body system. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h7)

question: What medical term describes abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Oligomenorrhea
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia refers specifically to menstrual periods with abnormally heavy or prolonged bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h2)

question: What are the two primary functions of the human nose?

options.A: Oxygenation and perfusion
options.B: Digestion and phonation
options.C: Respiration and olfaction
options.D: Filtration and circulation

explanation: The nose primarily functions as an airway for breathing (respiration) and as the sensory organ for smell (olfaction). [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: In some traditional Nigerian settings, how might hiring a paid home care nurse be viewed by the community?

options.A: As the cheapest way to manage chronic illness
options.B: As a mandatory legal requirement for all households
options.C: As a government-sponsored welfare program
options.D: As a sign of abandoning family care duties

explanation: You got it! Culturally, people sometimes wrongly assume hiring a nurse means you are neglecting your sick family member. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h5)

question: When must you use soap and water instead of an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Before entering every patient room
options.B: At the beginning and end of a nursing shift
options.C: When working in the emergency department
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Correct! Alcohol rubs are great, but they cannot cut through visible dirt or grime. When your hands look or feel dirty, good old soap and water is a must. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: Why is building an early, trusting relationship with an expectant mother so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the mother will have a completely pain-free labor
options.B: It encourages the mother to return for subsequent clinic visits
options.C: It completely eliminates all risks of genetic disorders in the fetus
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory tests during pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! When mothers trust us, they feel safe and are much more likely to keep coming back for their clinic check-ups, keeping both mum and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h1)

question: How are public health care providers mainly funded?

options.A: Direct patient user fees collected at each visit
options.B: Government tax revenues and public allocations
options.C: International NGO grants and foreign loans exclusively
options.D: Private donations and corporate investments only

explanation: Exactly! Public hospitals and clinics rely heavily on government budgets and taxes to keep their doors open for everyone. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why is feeling deeply distressed after a disaster considered a normal human reaction?

options.A: Because everyone experiences identical symptoms of grief
options.B: Because human brains are wired to ignore sudden changes
options.C: Because the event itself is abnormal and threatening to safety
options.D: Because medical treatment is rarely needed for shock

explanation: Spot on! It is completely normal to feel distressed when something terrifying and life-threatening happens around you. Your mind and body are just trying to process the shock. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which ethical principle guides a nurse's duty to act in the best interest of their psychiatric patient?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Beneficence is all about doing good and taking positive actions to care for and protect your patients. It's at the heart of nursing ethics! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h8)

question: What is the main focus of emergency nursing?

options.A: Providing long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Managing chronic lifestyle diseases at home
options.C: Conducting routine annual health screenings
options.D: Saving lives and stabilizing sudden illnesses

explanation: Emergency nurses specialize in immediate, acute interventions to stabilize patients facing life-threatening situations. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: To automatically prescribe medications without a doctor's order
options.B: To track the daily attendance and payroll of hospital staff
options.C: To store a comprehensive digital history of a patient's health information
options.D: To manage the public financial budget of the hospital

explanation: Correct! An EHR keeps all of a patient's medical history, test results, and treatments in one digital folder so authorized health workers can see them easily. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why are mid-range servers (minicomputers) so helpful in hospital departments like the laboratory?

options.A: They efficiently handle department-specific data traffic and device integration
options.B: They act as portable bedside charting tools for individual nurses
options.C: They predict global disease outbreaks using atmospheric data
options.D: They replace the need for electrical power outlets in the ward

explanation: You nailed it. Departments like the lab generate lots of specific results, and mid-range servers are perfect for managing that local workflow without slowing down the whole hospital. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which injection is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn from tetanus?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.C: Iron and folic acid tablets
options.D: Antimalarial drugs

explanation: Wonderful! Giving the tetanus toxoid vaccine to pregnant women helps build immunity that passes straight to the baby, keeping neonatal tetanus away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h2)
